# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why3: These are the two things I pitch: notes done during the walk instead of hours in the trailer, and texting the crew their items that day.
screens.why4: Two distinct rows, one gain each, no overlap, no number I did not write, and room to add up to four.
screens.why5: Both rows keep what I said, the 90% faster as hours back and texting the crew as same-day action items, and nothing of the product reaches the stranger.
screens.why7: The rows are noun phrases of what changes against today's way, my lead benefit is a row, both are kept and joined with 'and' in the belief, the hard case is the problem clause (hours on documents in the trailer) and not a routine occasion, and the card's fixed four-rung scale with 'I can't tell' tests it both ways.

screens.why1: After what it fits into and what it does better, asking what my supers have to take on to start using it is the obvious next question before I send anything out.
screens.why2: 'Setup, extra steps or learning' is how I'd talk about rolling a tool out to a super, and up to four at 9 words each is clear on first read.
screens.why3: I've watched supers walk sites and fight with Procore, so I know the efforts Fresco asks of them: narrating owners as they film and checking the notes before they go to the crew.
screens.why4: The only option besides my typed answer is the 'I'm not sure' chip, which fits a founder who can't name the effort and leaves the dimension out as the card says.
screens.why5: The box holds my two efforts in my own words, naming who owns each item as they film and checking the notes before they go out, so nothing has drifted.
screens.why7: The question asks for the effort these people take themselves, and my two rows are each one effort of at most 9 words, base-form verb phrases in their voice, the super's own step, not another role's sign-off, not Compatibility's phone-on-the-walk, and not Purchase friction's Procore check.

screens.why1: Right after I said what supers will have to do to start, checking what Keel wrote down as their efforts is the obvious next step before I pick one to test.
screens.why2: Naming who owns each item and checking notes before they go to the crew are plain to a super, though the intro repeats 'What they'll have to do' twice, which reads as a glitch.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does themselves on the walk or in the trailer: saying 'needs replacement by Alex' into the phone, and reading over notes before texting the crew.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, one during the walk and one after it, each a single step in a 'they' voice, with nothing silly and nothing doubled.
screens.why5: The first row is my narrated-assignee pitch ('needs replacement by Alex'), but 'check and fix the notes before they go out' is not something I typed, and it sits in the list as if it were mine.
screens.why7: Both rows are steps the super takes themselves and neither repeats Compatibility (filming and talking on the walk) or Purchase friction, but the second row reads as Keel's suggested new habit and is not marked as a suggestion or given its why, so the shape rule is bent.
screens.instead: What they'll have to do (under 9 words each, pick one to test): Name who owns each item as they film · [Keel suggests, last: Check and fix the notes before they go out -- why: an AI-written log the super signs has to be read first]

screens.why1: Right after I checked the steps Keel wrote from my answer, I pick the one effort strangers will be asked about, which is the obvious next move in the Solution step.
screens.why2: 'Name who owns each item as they film' and 'check and fix the notes before they go out' are how a super talks about punch items and the notes going to the crew and into Procore.
screens.why3: Both are things I watch supers do or skip on every walk, assigning an owner and proofing the notes, so I can weigh which would put them off from what I know.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts the super takes on themselves, in plain trade words, with no filler row and nothing missing that I typed.
screens.why5: Naming the owner as you film is my own pitch, the beam 'needs replacement by Alex' turned into an assignee, and the second row is the check a super makes before the notes go out, both kept as I'd say them.
screens.why7: Both rows are base-form efforts in one voice that the super takes themselves, with no sign-off, purchase step or Compatibility overlap, and the belief 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' can hold or fail on the yes-to-no item with its escape.

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out, asking whether to collect emails from supers who'd try it is the obvious last commercial choice, and I want those leads.
screens.why2: Offer a pilot, with the exact line people will see quoted, is plain to me on first read.
screens.why3: It is my own call about my own study, nothing I would have to guess at.
screens.why4: Yes or no is the whole choice, the two are distinct and in plain words, and no escape is needed for a founder's own decision.
screens.why5: The quoted line says 'try this for real' while I charge per site per month and the buyer is the GC, so a super leaving an email is a lead on the user side, not a paid site pilot; it drifts a little from what I'd call a pilot.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? Supers who say yes see: "Would you try this on your next site walk? Leave your email." — Yes, ask them / No pilot

screens.why1: Picking who fronts the interview is an obvious last step before the link goes out to my supers, and it comes right after the pilot offer.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint calls it a 'voice' while also saying the interviewer is on video. That leaves me unsure whether I'm picking a face, a voice or both, and the hint packs credits, recording and texting into one long paragraph.
screens.why3: I know how my supers talk and listen, and I can judge from a 5-second sample whether a voice will land with a super in a trailer at the end of the day.
screens.why4: Two names with samples cover the choice mechanically, but both read as women's voices, and for a mostly male trade I'd want at least one voice that sounds like it came off a jobsite.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product, price or buyer roles leaks into the interviewer choice, and the default pick is what I'd take.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? (Hint: the interviewer appears on video and speaks each question; every question is also on screen to tap or type. 400 credits either way.) Options: Daphne ▶ 5 s · Saskia ▶ 5 s · a plain-spoken male voice ▶ 5 s

screens.why1: After choosing who asks the questions and before sending, picking how supers will answer the link is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Plain words; "AI interviewer", "tap" and "link" read fine to me as a founder building an AI scribe.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on phones in a trailer or on site and can judge whether they'd rather tap or talk to a video.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct and complete, though "Read and tap" also allows speaking into boxes, so it partly overlaps the talking option; no escape is needed for a founder setting.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or roles leaks; it is a delivery choice and my pick "Read and tap" stands as typed.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how supers answer, the last step is who gets the link, which is exactly where I'd expect to decide whether I'm sending to supers I know or posting somewhere.
screens.why2: Plain English throughout; 'Contacts page' and 'open link' are clear enough to a founder in the flow, and nothing reads like another trade's jargon.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm reaching supers through intros from GCs I've met (my launch asked for exactly those) or through a list, so I can answer from what I actually do.
screens.why4: Three distinct ways to reach people — by name, from a Keel search, or one open link posted where supers already gather — cover the real routes, and no option overlaps or is missing for my case.
screens.why5: Nothing here alters my product or roles, and my pick — supers I know by name, each with their own link — is kept as typed.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right under the title with '4 counted' beside it, and each card shows '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know why there's no call: one person short on every belief.
screens.why_b2: There's no chart on the stage page, but the tally reads at once: 3 beliefs, all too few to call, 7 answered, 4 counted, and the bar is 5 needed.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility, Relative advantage and Adoption friction are my dimensions and the belief lines are recognisable, but they're reworded (the 'last day where they spent hours on documents in the trailer' line is clumsy), and the solution statement repeats itself ('turns them into notes with photos, assignees and due dates ... gets back notes with photos, assignees and due dates')
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: not that I'm one counted superintendent short per belief, not to send the study to more supers, not why 3 of my 7 weren't counted.
screens.why_b5: No claim goes past the data: n is shown (7 answered, 4 counted), and the low count is named as 'too few to call' rather than dressed up as a lean either way.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 7 superintendents counted on each belief and 5 are needed. 3 weren't counted because [reason]; send it to at least one more super on a commercial job to get a call on talking over videos on the walk, the hours back, and naming owners as they film.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count answers per option over 5 people with Luis set aside, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 mixes the floor of five with the 1-in-3 rule, and I had to look twice to see the marker is the count, not the bar.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and 'could talk into their phone over the noise on site' are my row as I saved it.
screens.why_b4: 'Ray's no is the one to ask about' names a person, but the card never says I need one more counted answer, or that 3 of 4 for would clear my 1-in-3 bar if it held.
screens.why_b5: The lean is honestly hedged, but the question asks about the noise on site on 'your last daily log', which happens in the trailer, not my site walk, and the closing schedule quote under Compatibility has nothing to do with talking over noise.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted say they could talk over the noise on their last site walk, 1 (Ray) could not, one more counted answer decides it; ask Ray what drowned him out.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know why it isn't called: Luis's guess left me one short of the floor.
screens.why_b2: The chart's 3 a lot / 0 a little / 1 same out of 4 reads quickly, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 mixes the five-person floor with my 1-in-3 bar, and on first look it reads like '4 of 5 for me'.
screens.why_b3: The belief is mine: the hours in the trailer after the walks, giving them hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day; only the bar line's 'You said hours back at the end of the day' drops my second benefit.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted answer would decide it, or that the lean so far is 3 of 4 a lot better, with only Denise's no difference against, and hers because her log is already done on the tablet.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted), the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and nothing is claimed past the four, though the count line's 'about their last daily log' doesn't quite match the trailer-day question that was actually asked.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 said a lot better and 1 (Denise, who finishes her log on the tablet) said no difference, which is under your 1-in-3 bar; one more counted answer decides it.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know where this stands and why.
screens.why_b2: The chart plainly counts each answer over 5 people, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' sits beside a rule of 'no more than 1 in 3 say probably not or no', so I have to look twice to see the bar is 5 counted and not 4 of 5 saying yes.
screens.why_b3: Adoption friction and 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' are the effort and belief I picked, and the asked clause is the one I wrote for the superintendents.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me to get one more superintendent counted, or that two of my three yeses hang on naming owners not slowing the walk, which is what I would design for.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, Luis's guess is set apart by name, the conditional yeses are split out, and a 3-for-1 result is called 'a lean, not a call' rather than a hold.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 counted, 5 needed, with 3 for and 1 against so far. Two of the three yeses hinge on it keeping the walk moving, so make naming an owner a few words said mid-video, and get one more superintendent's answer to call it.

screens.why_b1: Each box says 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right under it, so I know there's no call yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: The Compatibility line is the one I checked, talking into the phone over site noise, but the Relative advantage line is my two benefits forced into a broken template ('For most, with it, their last day where...') that I recognise but would never say.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need another answer, but nothing says what these two 'against' answers mean for filming on the walk or for the hours-back pitch.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible on both lines, the low count is named as too few to call, and each quote is labelled as one person's against with nothing claimed beyond it.
screens.why_b6: Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' and Denise's 'done on the tablet before I leave the gate' tell me the log isn't the fire for some supes; subs and the schedule are, which cuts against both my noise belief and my hours-back pitch.
screens.instead: Too few to call (4 of 5): one more answer settles each line. So far the two 'no's aren't about noise or the tool. Ray puts the log behind a slipping schedule, and Denise finishes hers on the tablet before the gate, so ask the next supes whether the log is what eats their evening at all.

screens.why1: First screen, and it checks the one thing that matters for the rest: whether my jobs keep their dailies in Procore or something like it.
screens.why2: I'd answer it right away, but nobody on my site says 'construction project management system'; we say Procore or ACC, so naming them would land quicker.
screens.why3: I know exactly where my daily logs go on every job I'm running, so this is straight from my own day.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it cleanly for a gate, and a gate needs no escape.
screens.why5: Nothing about the founder's product or plan comes through; it only asks where my logs live, which is the founder's segment of Procore or ACC jobs put in neutral terms.
screens.why6: It's one short question with two options, but 'construction project management system' is a four-word mouthful to hear once, and naming Procore or ACC would say better.
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you're running now keep their daily logs in Procore, ACC or similar software? Yes · No

screens.why1: After asking whether my jobs run their logs in Procore, asking whether I had the end-of-day log grind this week is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: 'Finish photos' isn't how I'd say it, since I take photos and upload them, and photos and daily logs joined together makes it a two-part question on first hearing.
screens.why3: Whether I sat in the trailer this week getting photos into Procore and the log done is exactly what I know.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this gate.
screens.why5: The cost is the hours of uploading and typing after the walks, but the screen asks where I finished it ('in the trailer'), so it drifted a little from the problem toward the place.
screens.why6: Short, one question, 'Yes or no.' at the end, easy to answer on one hearing.
screens.why7: It sits close to the routine, because almost every super finishes the log in the trailer, and a super who struggled through it at home that night would truly say No, so the No side doesn't cleanly mean 'didn't have the problem'.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you spend time after your walks uploading photos and typing up the daily log? Yes or no.

screens.why1: After two questions about my daily logs and photos, showing me the idea before Part 2 is the obvious next step, even if it leans more toward walk notes and punch items than the daily log itself.
screens.why2: Site walk, assignees, Procore and ACC are all words I use every day; "AI scribe" isn't my word, but I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day, take photos and hand out items to the subs, so I can picture exactly where this would fit in my day.
screens.why4: A card to read; it shows no options.
screens.why5: The belief line repeats the first line ("turns what you say into notes and action items") instead of saying what it gets me, and it drifts from what Part 1 asked about (getting the photos and daily log done) toward crew action items.
screens.why6: It can be said, but the how-it-works part runs four sentences and "notes and action items" comes three times, so by the belief line I'm hearing the same thing again.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an AI scribe for site walks. You take short videos and talk over them; it writes up notes with photos, who's on it and when it's due, texts the crew their items, and sends it all to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would get your daily log done without the hours in the trailer after the walk.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card it makes sense to ask whether I could even talk into my phone on a walk, since the whole idea rests on filming and talking as I go.
screens.why2: Talking into my phone over the noise on site is plain jobsite talk, and I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I talk on the walk and write the daily log in the trailer, so 'your last daily log' makes me work back to the walk that fed it before I can answer about the noise out there.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, only sometimes and no cover it: some days the saws and the pump truck drown me out and some days they don't, and 'I can't tell' fits for a day I never tried.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks past the idea card shown on purpose; the question is about my noise and my phone, not the product's own terms.
screens.why6: It's short and one question, and four short options plus 'you can't tell' are easy to hold by ear.
screens.why7: It's an ability with the four ability rungs in order and 'I can't tell' apart, and it tests the step the pitch rests on (talking on site), which is true for some supers and not others, so the belief can hold or fail.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily · Yes, most of the time · Only sometimes · No · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after I've seen what Fresco is and been asked whether I could talk into my phone on site, asking whether it would have beaten my own trailer evening is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: Uploading photos, typing logs and the trailer are my everyday words, and 'AI scribe' was just explained on the card above, so I can answer it on first read.
screens.why3: I know exactly the day I sat in the trailer for hours pushing photos into Procore and writing up the log, so I can judge this from my own week.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference and worse cover every answer I could give without overlapping, and 'I can't tell' fits if I can't picture it working on my site.
screens.why5: The hard case is my own pain, the hours in the trailer, and nothing about Fresco reaches me beyond the idea card I was meant to see.
screens.why6: Heard aloud it is one short scene and one short question, then four short options and one escape, so I can hold it all and answer.
screens.why7: It has the four fixed rungs in order with two for and two against, names no benefit of the founder's, sets it on the day the job hurt rather than any last day, and has the single 'I can't tell' escape apart.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether it would beat my evenings in the trailer, it makes sense to ask what extra work it would put on me during the walk itself.
screens.why2: I'd follow it, but 'who owns each item' isn't how I talk on a walk; I'd say which sub it's on, or whose court the ball is in, so it takes a second read.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day and already tell the subs what's on them, so I know whether I'd call that out while filming.
screens.why4: Yes, a real 'only if' about not slowing my walk, probably not and no are distinct and cover my true answer, and 'I can't tell' fits as the way out.
screens.why5: Beyond the idea card I was meant to see, nothing leaks; naming who's responsible as I film is a plain step I'd take myself, not the founder's inside terms.
screens.why6: Heard once it's short and one question, and four short options plus 'you can't tell' are easy to hold.
screens.why7: The effort is a new habit I'd take myself on every walk, the condition is my own assurance rather than a fear, the options run two for and two against, and 'I can't tell' sits apart as the card requires.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd say which sub each item is on as you film. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Only if it keeps the walk moving · Probably not · No · I can't tell
